scope: Corollary 5.1 (Weighted second-neighborhood forms) of the manuscript “A proof of Seymour’s second-neighborhood conjecture” (preprints/A-proof-of-Seymours-second-neighborhood-conjecture-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 173 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 20be859799f83e34), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 12-13. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let D be a nonempty finite oriented graph, and write A(D) for its arc set. For a vertex weighting η : V (D) → [0, ∞), write η(S) = P x∈S η(x). Then the following hold. (i) For every vertex weighting η : V (D) → [0, ∞), there is a vertex v ∈ V (D) such that η(N+ 1 (v)) ≤ η(N+ 2 (v)). (ii) There is a vertex weighting η : V (D) → [0, ∞) with P x∈V (D) η(x) = 1 such that η(N+ 1 (v)) ≤ η(N+ 2 (v)) for every v ∈ V (D). The entries of this weighting need not all be positive. (iii) For every arc weighting w : A(D) → [0, ∞), extend the notation by setting w(vs) = 0 when vs / ∈ A(D). For v, s ∈ V (D), put βw v (s) = max ( {0} ∪ {w(us) − w(vs) : u ∈ V (D), v → u → s} ) . 12 Then there is a vertex v ∈ V (D) such that X s∈V (D) βw v (s) ≥ X u∈N+ 1 (v) w(vu). The maximum is zero if there is no indicated two-step path. Such paths are determined by the arcs of D, so an arc of weight zero is still present and is not treated as a missing arc.
